before.title: Daunomustine chemotherapy for treatment-naive canine multicentric lymphoma
before.center: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
before.status: Currently listed as a funded canine lymphoma study by the University of Illinois
before.funding: Study treatment and study visits are fully funded after eligibility is established. Owners pay the initial examination and eligibility diagnostics, unrelated care and uncovered adverse-event costs. The consultation is approximately $250, excluding diagnostics, medication and treatment. Partial adverse-event funding is available for care at Illinois. A $1,000 Illinois hospital credit is provided after completion or removal for stable/progressive disease.
before.special_requirement: Peripheral-node multicentric lymphoma only; indolent and small-cell lymphoma are excluded. No previous chemotherapy or systemic steroid therapy; steroid-containing topical products are allowed. Organ function, blood counts and cardiac eligibility require study-team review.
before.notes: Up to five intravenous daunomustine doses every 14 days, with response-guided within-patient dose escalation and examinations/bloodwork seven days after treatment. A single L-asparaginase dose may be added for dogs not in complete remission. Dogs with progressive disease leave the trial and are offered standard care. Long-term visits follow the treatment course. Initial eligibility testing and unrelated care remain owner-paid; participation does not guarantee response.

before.title: SBRT plus dendritic-cell homing hydrogel for canine appendicular osteosarcoma
before.center: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
before.status: Currently listed as a funded clinical trial on the Illinois master roster
before.contacts: Rebecca Kamerer, Clinical Trials Coordinator — rmoss81@illinois.edu; 217-300-6453. Appointments: 217-333-5300.
before.funding: Fully funded after eligibility: CT, biopsy, three-day SBRT, hydrogel injection, study recheck exams and bloodwork. Owners pay the initial consultation (approximately $250), eligibility diagnostics, pain medication and unrelated care.
before.notes: Individual current official PDF read in full October 14, 2026. Dogs strictly older than one year, at least 5 kg, with histologic or cytologic alkaline-phosphatase-positive appendicular osteosarcoma; no chest/abdominal metastasis, no previous chemotherapy, radiation or immunotherapy. No Apoquel, topical/systemic steroids or immune modulators within 14 days. Adequate organ function for sedation; significant preexisting renal/hepatic/cardiac disease and autoimmune history exclude entry. Eligibility diagnostics within 14 days. CT and tumor biopsy under anesthesia, SBRT on three consecutive days, then peritumoral DC-homing hydrogel immediately after the third fraction. Blood sampling four days later and weekly follow-up for five weeks; other traditional treatments may follow completion. This is distinct from the JEN-101/radiation protocol requiring amputation.
before.intervention: Three consecutive days of SBRT followed by local dendritic-cell homing hydrogel; weekly follow-up for five weeks

sites.hospital: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
sites.name: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital

before.special_requirement: Strictly age >1 year and weight ≥5 kg; nonmetastatic appendicular OSA. No prior radiation, chemo or immunotherapy; 14-day washout for Apoquel/steroids/immune modulators. Team must confirm anesthetic fitness, organ disease, autoimmune history and staging. Amputation is not a mandatory part of this separate SBRT/hydrogel protocol.

before.title: Intravenous Z-007 immune-stimulatory nanoparticle for canine osteosarcoma with pulmonary metastases
before.contacts: Rebecca Kamerer, Clinical Trials Coordinator — rmoss81@illinois.edu · 217-300-6453; appointments 217-333-5300
before.funding: Fully funded after eligibility: trial exams, bloodwork, Z-007 administration and CT scans are covered. Owner pays the initial exam and eligibility diagnostics.
before.notes: Historical or active osteosarcoma from any primary site, confirmed by histopathology or cytology, with pulmonary nodules at least 5 mm on CT. If the primary tumor has not been amputated, its pain must be controlled. Requires good general condition and expected survival of at least nine weeks. Pleural effusion, hypoxia or respiratory distress exclude participation. Radiation requires at least a one-week washout; chemotherapy or immunotherapy requires at least three weeks. Concurrent immunosuppressive medication, including cyclosporine, Apoquel or immunosuppressive steroid doses, is not allowed. The current October 2026 protocol specifies up to eight weekly intravenous Z-007 doses, baseline and week-9 CT, and possible discretionary compassionate continuation only for objective response. Study exams, bloodwork, drug administration and CT are funded after eligibility; screening and unrelated care are owner-paid.
before.intervention: Up to eight once-weekly intravenous doses of Z-007 with baseline and week-9 CT; compassionate continuation may be offered for objective response

sites.hospital: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital
sites.name: University of Illinois Veterinary Teaching Hospital

before.special_requirement: Osteosarcoma from any primary site with lung nodules at least 5 mm on CT. The study team must confirm radiation washout of at least one week and chemotherapy/immunotherapy washout of at least three weeks, controlled primary-tumor pain if not amputated, general health and expected survival of at least nine weeks. Pleural effusion, hypoxia or respiratory distress exclude enrollment; concurrent immunosuppressive drugs are prohibited.

before.title: Polymer-conjugated pirarubicin for advanced canine solid tumors
before.center: University of Tokyo Veterinary Medical Center
before.status: Currently enrolling on the official clinical-research page
before.contacts: University of Tokyo Veterinary Medical Center — 03-5841-5420
before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. The investigational drug is provided at no charge; owners should confirm screening and routine-care costs with the center.
before.notes: Dogs need an unresectable or metastatic malignant solid tumor for which other radiation or anticancer-drug options are not expected to be effective or have failed. The investigational macromolecular anticancer agent links pirarubicin to a polymer and is administered intravenously every two weeks. Visits are required every one to two weeks and owners must permit lesion sampling. Final tumor-type and medical eligibility are individualized by the study team.

before.title: Lapatinib for feline transitional cell carcinoma
before.center: University of Tokyo Veterinary Medical Center
before.status: Currently enrolling on the official clinical-research page
before.contacts: University of Tokyo Veterinary Medical Center — 03-5841-5420
before.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. The official page states that part of the study-drug cost is waived; owners should confirm other clinical costs with the center.
before.notes: Veterinarian-led trial for cats diagnosed or suspected to have bladder or urethral transitional cell carcinoma. Cats must not have received chemotherapy, radiation or tumor-removal surgery; NSAIDs are allowed. Owners give oral lapatinib once daily and return to Tokyo approximately every four weeks for response and safety assessment.

after.funding: 🟡 Partially funded. The official page states that part of the study-drug cost is waived; owners should confirm other clinical costs with the center.
after.notes: Veterinarian-led trial for cats diagnosed or suspected to have bladder or urethral transitional cell carcinoma. Cats must not have received chemotherapy, radiation or tumor-removal surgery; NSAIDs are allowed. Owners give oral lapatinib once daily and return to Tokyo approximately every four weeks for response and safety assessment. The current official organizer notice states that the target case count has been reached and the trial will end on October 31, 2026. It separately offers drug use at owner expense. Preserve this as treatment-access information, not an open recruiting study; no separate access record is created without evaluating that category.
